slides.headline: The Everglades is actually a RIVER
It's up to 30 miles wide
slides.body: A shallow sheet of water flowing through sawgrass: the river of grass.

slides.headline: It moves about 100 feet a day
slides.body: That's in winter. In the wet summer it can reach about a mile a day.

slides.headline: Its slope is under 2 inches per mile
slides.body: Water spills over from Lake Okeechobee and creeps south anyway.

slides.headline: It flows about 100 miles
slides.body: From Lake Okeechobee all the way down to Florida Bay.

slides.headline: Less than half of it is left
slides.body: Drainage shrank the original Everglades. The national park has protected its south end since 1947.
